newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SingTel falls, eyes support at S$2.50.
newsitem.headline: SingTel falls, eyes support at S$2.50.

text.p: Singapore Telecom (SingTel) shares fell in active dealings on Tuesday touching a 20-month low of Singapore $2.65.
The last time SingTel shares were at S$2.65 was on August 15 1995. At 0415 GMT, SingTel was down six cents to S$2.66. Volume was an active 3.2 million shares.
Dealers said SingTel shares have been falling since it lost its monopoly on the Singapore telecommunications market on April 1.
"The share is still as expensive compared with other telecom stocks. But it could see some support at S$2.50," said a dealer with a Singapore brokerage.

Analysts said the S$2.50 level could provide support as that was the price of the second public offer of SingTel shares from the government, which still holds more than 80 percent of the telecommunications company, to Singaporeans.
The second public offer last year had a loyalty bonus scheme to encourage Singaporean shareholders to hold onto their shares.
